title: Quiz Adaptive Layout
description: Make the quiz client far more adaptive to width and device: desktop, tablet and mobile are each laid out by hand. An element that fits on one line uses the left and the right of it (e.g. a classification item with its dropdown beside it) and breaks onto two lines only where there is no room, such as on a phone.
note: Ticket bookkeeping manual on disk: repo MCP (CONNECTION_CLOSED) and semio MCP (CONNECT_TIMEOUT) failed to connect on 2026-10-02. Closed manually on 2026-10-03 (repo MCP still down).
summary: Every part of the quiz client now lays itself out for the room it has — its card, task or list, measured by container queries in rem so larger text gets the narrower layout — instead of the window. Classification items, sorting rows and matching rows stand on one line (label left, select/guess/buttons right, selects aligned) where they fit and on two lines only where they do not; wide tasks put the pool or the value cards beside what they are dropped on; the run head lists its tasks on phones, shows chips on tablets and puts the progress beside them on desktops; preferences and the ways to appear get aligned columns; touch gets 40 px task targets. Every table (results, leaderboard page and card, learner runs, radar values) folds into labelled records below the width its columns need, keeping its table roles, and crowd figures fold item-over-columns, so nothing scrolls sideways at 320–1920 px or at 1.5× text. Matching became a list of rows, the sorting row's source order matches its reading order, the drag ghost keeps its row shape, list-mode overview cards got a fixed reading width, and runs/results use up to 100 rem of large screens. Tiers are shared vectors held against the stylesheet by lightningcss (unit) and walked on a phone, a tablet and two desktops in a real browser (e2e project `layout`, 4/4 passed). See 📓️adaptive-layout-report.md; the remaining suite and typecheck failures belong to a concurrent session's unfinished challenge work.
